subject: Fraud & Scams
title: Churning: When Your Broker Is the Scammer
description: A 1-minute de-risking session on Churning: When Your Broker Is the Scammer.

hook.text: Your financial advisor makes 200 trades a year in your account. Each trade earns them a commission.

buildup.text: Churning means excessive trading designed to generate commissions, not returns for the client.

discovery.text: The client's portfolio may break even or lose money — while the broker earns thousands in fees.

twist.text: Churning is hard to detect because victims assume their advisor is trading for good reasons.

climax.text: FINRA regularly fines and bars brokers for churning, but many victims never file complaints.

punchline.text: Every trade cost you money — and made your advisor richer.

quiz.question: What is churning in investment fraud?
options: Excessive trading to generate broker commissions
Rapid buying and selling by day traders
